intent.goal: Read WIP-curve evidence only from the report's WIP-curve section, so a complete-looking wave= row quoted in a fenced example, a deviations table or another section can neither bind as the run's evidence nor trip the duplicate/stray/unmeasured-row checks against the real rows, while every per-wave completeness check keeps running on the section's rows.
intent.ruled_out: Requiring the full template heading text (the module's own '## WIP curve' fixtures, used by every pre-existing WIP-curve test, would stop opening the section, and the 2026-08-28 ship-it report's heading differs after 'row'); matching any heading that merely CONTAINS 'WIP-curve' (a '## Deviations — WIP-curve notes' section would open it); falling back to whole-document scanning when no section exists (the false pass C-1 names returns for a report with no section at all); ending the section only at a heading of the same or higher level (a '### ...' subsection would then silently extend it); changes to WIP caps, graduation analysis or the other report checks (spec out of scope).
intent.why: The template already names the section, and both the template and the one real report open it with an ATX heading whose text begins 'WIP-curve'. Opening on a heading that BEGINS by naming the WIP curve (whitespace and case tolerant), closing on the next heading of any kind, and skipping fenced code with the CommonMark closing rule accepts every heading the repository actually uses and nothing that merely mentions the curve. Scoping happens in the line source of _wip_rows, so the completeness checks downstream are untouched.
